h1_old: How to Dismiss a Traffic Ticket in Lubbock with Defensive Driving

faqs.q: How much does it cost to dismiss a ticket in Lubbock?
faqs.a: The court cost is typically up to about $144 ($169 in a school zone), set by each court — some Lubbock-area courts charge less (Slaton and Wolfforth post $144). The TDLR-approved course is separate; ours is $28. Check your court's page for the exact amount.

faqs.q: Can I take the Lubbock defensive driving course online?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the court approves your request, a TDLR-approved 6-hour course can be completed fully online. Every Lubbock-area court accepts a state-approved online course.

faqs.q: My ticket is from Wolfforth / Shallowater / Slaton, not Lubbock. Does that change things?
faqs.a: The legal steps are the same, but you deal with that city's court — each with its own fee, request method, and deadlines. Open its page in the table above.

faqs.q: How long do I have to finish?
faqs.a: Generally 90 days after the court approves the request. Request the course by your appearance date first, and don't pay the ticket — paying is a guilty plea and a conviction.

faqs.q: Does a dismissal keep it off my insurance?
faqs.a: Yes. A driving safety course dismissal keeps the charge off your driving record under Texas law, so it can't raise your insurance — unlike paying, which is a conviction.

courts.name: Lubbock Municipal Court
courts.note: You'll need a certified Type 3A driving record from Texas DPS — most drivers do not have this ready.
